title: Descent in the bottom supported degree of a smooth pair
statement:
Use the finite datum $k,\ell,E,n,A$ of [def-pur-conventions], for arbitrary $n\geq1$. Let $V\to B$ be a smooth morphism of $k$-schemes, of a fixed finite relative dimension [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], let $Z\hookrightarrow V$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $Z\to B$ smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let it have pure codimension $c\geq0$ in the sense of [def-pur-frame-class]: $\dim\mathcal O_{V,z}=\dim\mathcal O_{Z,z}+c$ for every $z\in Z$, with Krull dimension the supremum of lengths of strict chains of prime ideals. Let $e:U\to V$ be etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and suppose the ideal of $Z_U=Z\times_V U$ in $U$ is generated by $c$ global functions, as for a frame in [def-pur-frame-class]. Fix $r\in\mathbf Z$. On the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] of $U$, with the twists $A(r)$ of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], let $\underline\Gamma_{Z_U}$ be the subsheaf-of-sections functor with support [def-pur-etale-supported-kernel] and let $R\underline\Gamma_{Z_U}$ be its right derived functor (these sheaves live on $U$ and vanish off $Z_U$). Write $\mathcal H^b_{Z_U}(A(r))$ for its cohomology sheaves. Then
$$\mathcal H^b_{Z_U}(A(r))=0\quad(b<2c).$$
The canonical local-to-global edge map [def-pur-grothendieck-edge-maps] identifies
$$H^{2c}_{Z_U\times_U W}(W,A(r))\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma\bigl(W,\mathcal H^{2c}_{Z_U}(A(r))|_W\bigr)$$
for every etale $W\to U$, naturally under further etale restriction. Here the left side is [def-pur-support-cohomology]. The same assertion about the left side holds when it is computed on the small pro-etale site $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], using its canonical comparison with ordinary etale supported cohomology. Consequently, if two classes in $H^{2c}_{Z_U}(U,A(r))$ have equal restrictions on every member of an etale covering of $U$, they are equal. No identification of the degree-$2c$ sheaf with a constant or twist sheaf, and no frame class or orientation, is asserted. The underlying abelian sheaf of a module coefficient sheaf is given by sectionwise scalar forgetting [def-pur-etale-module-abelian-forget].

source.place: Tag 09XP, section-cohomology-support: sheaf supported functor and local-to-global spectral sequence. Lower-degree vanishing is an agent-formulated relative smooth-pair refinement: use etale coordinates of Tag 0FUE (more-morphisms.tex) and the coordinate zero-section calculation of the affine-line route. Milne, Lectures on Etale Cohomology, Section 16, Theorem 16.7 and Lemma 16.8 explain the analogous smooth-field pair calculation; that field-only theorem is not cited as the relative-base assertion.

proof.text: For $c=0$, the empty tuple generates the zero ideal, so $Z_U=U$ and supported sections are ordinary sections by [def-pur-support-cohomology]. The derived sheaf-of-supported-sections functor is then the identity, so its negative cohomology sheaves vanish and its degree-zero edge is the identity on sections. Assume $c>0$ in Steps 2--7; Step 8 also supplies the pro-etale assertion for $c=0$.

source.place: The c=0 boundary case from the support definition.

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $\bar u$ on $Z_U$. Apply [lem-pur-smooth-pair-local-coordinates] to $(V,Z)$ at its image to obtain an open chart $U_0\subseteq V$ etale over $\mathbf A^{a+b}_B$, with $Z\cap U_0$ the inverse image of the coordinate subspace. Pull back to $T=U\times_VU_0$, an open neighbourhood of $\bar u$ in $U$. Its composite coordinate map is etale and its support is the same coordinate inverse image. Restriction to the open $T$ is exact and preserves injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives], and the underived support functor commutes with it (both assign $\ker(F(W)\to F(W\setminus Z_W))$ to an etale $W\to T$), so $R\underline\Gamma_{Z_U}(A(r))|_T\simeq R\underline\Gamma_{Z_T}(A(r))$ and the geometric stalks at $\bar u$ agree. Apply [lem-pur-relative-support-coordinate-model] with $X=V$, $Y=Z$, $S=B$, and this $T$. The hypothesis $\dim\mathcal O_{V,z}=\dim\mathcal O_{Z,z}+c$ holds at every $z\in Z$, so its final clause gives $b=c$. Its comparison identifies the geometric supported stalk with $R\Gamma_{\{0\}}(\mathbf A^c_k,A(r))$, on the ordinary etale site. This local comparison is the new geometric input; it is not inferred from a calculation merely on a geometric fibre.

source.place: Local smooth-pair coordinates and pure-codimension reduction.

proof.text: Compute the field model of Step 2 over the fixed algebraically closed field $k$. Put $C_1=R\Gamma_{\{0\}}(\mathbf A^1_k,A(1))$. By [thm-pur-rank-one-local-calculation], its only cohomology is $H^2(C_1)\cong A$; negative degrees vanish because a sheaf is resolved in nonnegative degrees. Thus truncation gives $C_1\simeq A[-2]$. Iterating [lem-pur-kunneth-supported] on the separated finite-type $k$-schemes $\mathbf A^j_k$ identifies $R\Gamma_{\{0\}}(\mathbf A^c_k,A(c))$ with $C_1^{\otimes_A^L c}\simeq A[-2c]$. The coefficients are finite-Tor because their twists are locally free rank-one sheaves by [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] and the twist tensor/inverse formulas of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. For general $r$, trivialize the one-dimensional coefficient line $A(r-c)$ over the algebraically closed field $k$; its tensor with $A(c)$ is $A(r)$ by that definition. This gives the same vanishing below $2c$, independently of the chosen trivialization. There are no extra negative Tor terms: every factor after truncation is a shift of the free module $A$. Via Step 2 and [lem-kun-stalks-of-cohomology], all geometric stalks of $\mathcal H^b_{Z_U}(A(r))$ vanish for $b<2c$ on the support; off the support the defining kernel functor is zero locally, so the same holds there. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] to $0\to\mathcal H^b_{Z_U}(A(r))$ to conclude the sheaf is zero.

source.place: Rank-one Kummer calculation, supported product, and geometric-stalk conservativity.

proof.text: Put $i:Z_U\hookrightarrow U$, $j:U\setminus Z_U\hookrightarrow U$, and $P(F)=\ker(F\to j_*j^*F)$. By [lem-pur-etale-supported-kernel-adjunction], $P=i_*i^!_0$, with $i_*$ exact and left adjoint to $i^!_0$. Apply [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] to obtain that $i^!_0$ sends injectives to injectives. By [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-preserves-injectives], $i_*$ also sends injectives to injectives. Thus $P$ sends injectives to injectives. This isolates the closed-support adjunction and the acyclicity needed for the next step.

source.place: Tag 09XP, section-cohomology-support; Tag 09XQ, lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic; Tag 015N, lemma-grothendieck-spectral-sequence. The support acyclicity check and restriction naturality are written out.

proof.text: For an etale $W\to U$ take $G_W(F)=\Gamma(W,F|_W)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives], restriction preserves injectives, so $R^pG_W(F)=H^p(W,F|_W)$. The preceding step makes $P(I)$ injective, hence $G_W$-acyclic, for each injective $I$. The composite $G_WP$ is precisely the supported-sections functor [def-pur-support-cohomology], since its sections are the kernel of restriction to $W\setminus(Z_U\times_UW)$. Apply [thm-sp-grothendieck] to obtain the first-quadrant spectral sequence $E_2^{p,q}=H^p(W,\mathcal H^q_{Z_U}(A(r))|_W)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}_{Z_U\times_UW}(W,A(r))$.

source.place: Tag 09XP, section-cohomology-support; Tag 09XQ, lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic; Tag 015N, lemma-grothendieck-spectral-sequence. The support acyclicity check and restriction naturality are written out.

proof.text: Step 3 gives $E_2^{p,q}=0$ for $q<2c$. The spectral sequence of [thm-sp-grothendieck] just constructed is first-quadrant and converges to $H^n=H^n_{Z_U\times_UW}(W,A(r))$ with a finite filtration whose graded pieces are $E_\infty^{p,n-p}$; these vanish for $p<0$ and $p>n$, so $F^0H^n=H^n$ and $F^{n+1}H^n=0$. Apply [lem-pur-first-quadrant-lowest-row-edge] with $m=2c$. Its canonical left edge is the required isomorphism $H^{2c}_{Z_U\times_UW}(W,A(r))\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(W,\mathcal H^{2c}_{Z_U}(A(r))|_W)$. The left edge is the canonical composite through the abutment filtration and the source/target derived-functor identifications of [lem-sp-grothendieck-edge-maps]; thus the lowest-row argument applies to this specified map.

source.place: Tag 09XP, section-cohomology-support; Tag 09XQ, lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic; Tag 015N, lemma-grothendieck-spectral-sequence. The support acyclicity check and restriction naturality are written out.

proof.text: For restriction compatibility, use [lem-pc-grothendieck-edge-cocycle] with the same injective resolution $A(r)\to I^\bullet$ on $U$ for every $W$. It describes the edge by the map from a cocycle in $\Gamma(W,P(I^\bullet)|_W)$ to its section of $\mathcal H^{2c}(P(I^\bullet))|_W$. For a further etale map $W^\prime\to W$, the cycles-to-cohomology quotient is a morphism of sheaves, so its maps on sections commute with restriction. Hence the two edge maps commute with restriction. This uses the existing cocycle statement rather than assuming functoriality in the second functor of the Grothendieck spectral sequence.

source.place: Tag 09XP, section-cohomology-support; Tag 09XQ, lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic; Tag 015N, lemma-grothendieck-spectral-sequence. The support acyclicity check and restriction naturality are written out.

proof.text: For each etale $W\to U$, set $C=Z_U\times_UW$ and $O=W\setminus C$. Apply [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] both on $W$ and on $O$. The derived unit identifies the ordinary etale and pro-etale cohomology of the finite coefficient sheaf $A(r)$ on each, compatibly with restriction. The functorial support long exact sequences on both sites in [thm-pur-with-support-exactness] now form a commutative diagram. In the five-term segment $H^{d-1}(W)\to H^{d-1}(O)\to H^d_C(W)\to H^d(W)\to H^d(O)$, all four ordinary-cohomology comparison arrows are isomorphisms; the five lemma gives the middle supported comparison. Taking $d=2c$ transfers the edge isomorphism of Step 6 (or Step 1) to the pro-etale left side. Naturality of the unit and support sequences makes this comparison commute with every further etale restriction. The coefficient convention commutes with derived direct image along the open complement by [lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-derived-direct-image-comparison], so forgetting scalars is compatible with the localization triangles defining this support comparison.

source.place: Etale/pro-etale comparison for finite coefficients.

proof.text: Let two degree-$2c$ supported classes have equal restrictions to an etale covering of $U$. By the natural edge isomorphism in Step 6 (Step 1 if $c=0$), their images are sections of $\mathcal H^{2c}_{Z_U}(A(r))$ agreeing on that cover. The sheaf separation axiom makes the images equal globally; injectivity of the edge makes the original classes equal. No identification of this sheaf with a constant or twist sheaf, and no orientation or frame-independence assertion, is used.

source.place: Final etale-cover equality consequence.

Iterating [lem-pur-kunneth-supported] on the separated finite-type $k$-schemes $\mathbf A^j_k$ identifies $R\Gamma_{\{0\}}(\mathbf A^c_k,A(c))$ with $C_1^{\otimes_A^L c}\simeq A[-2c]$. The coefficients are finite-Tor because their twists are locally free rank-one sheaves by [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] and the twist tensor/inverse formulas of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. For general $r$, trivialize the one-dimensional coefficient line $A(r-c)$ over the algebraically closed field $k$; its tensor with $A(c)$ is $A(r)$ by that definition. This gives the same vanishing below $2c$, independently of the chosen trivialization. There are no extra negative Tor terms: every factor after truncation is a shift of the free module $A$. Via Step 2 and [lem-kun-stalks-of-cohomology], all geometric stalks of $\mathcal H^b_{Z_U}(A(r))$ vanish for $b<2c$ on the support; off the support the defining kernel functor is zero locally, so the same holds there. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] to $0\to\mathcal H^b_{Z_U}(A(r))$ to conclude the sheaf is zero.

old_proof.text: Put $i:Z_U\hookrightarrow U$, $j:U\setminus Z_U\hookrightarrow U$, and $P(F)=\ker(F\to j_*j^*F)$. By [lem-pur-etale-supported-kernel-adjunction], $P=i_*i^!_0$, with $i_*$ exact and left adjoint to $i^!_0$. Apply [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] to obtain that $i^!_0$ sends injectives to injectives. By [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-preserves-injectives], $i_*$ also sends injectives to injectives. Thus $P$ sends injectives to injectives. This isolates the closed-support adjunction and the acyclicity needed for the next step.

old_proof.text: For an etale $W\to U$ take $G_W(F)=\Gamma(W,F|_W)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives], restriction preserves injectives, so $R^pG_W(F)=H^p(W,F|_W)$. The preceding step makes $P(I)$ injective, hence $G_W$-acyclic, for each injective $I$. The composite $G_WP$ is precisely the supported-sections functor [def-pur-support-cohomology], since its sections are the kernel of restriction to $W\setminus(Z_U\times_UW)$. Apply [thm-sp-grothendieck] to obtain the first-quadrant spectral sequence $E_2^{p,q}=H^p(W,\mathcal H^q_{Z_U}(A(r))|_W)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}_{Z_U\times_UW}(W,A(r))$.

old_proof.text: Step 3 gives $E_2^{p,q}=0$ for $q<2c$. The spectral sequence of [thm-sp-grothendieck] just constructed is first-quadrant and converges to $H^n=H^n_{Z_U\times_UW}(W,A(r))$ with a finite filtration whose graded pieces are $E_\infty^{p,n-p}$; these vanish for $p<0$ and $p>n$, so $F^0H^n=H^n$ and $F^{n+1}H^n=0$. Apply [lem-pur-first-quadrant-lowest-row-edge] with $m=2c$. Its canonical left edge is the required isomorphism $H^{2c}_{Z_U\times_UW}(W,A(r))\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(W,\mathcal H^{2c}_{Z_U}(A(r))|_W)$.

old_proof.text: For restriction compatibility, use [lem-pc-grothendieck-edge-cocycle] with the same injective resolution $A(r)\to I^\bullet$ on $U$ for every $W$. It describes the edge by the map from a cocycle in $\Gamma(W,P(I^\bullet)|_W)$ to its section of $\mathcal H^{2c}(P(I^\bullet))|_W$. For a further etale map $W^\prime\to W$, the cycles-to-cohomology quotient is a morphism of sheaves, so its maps on sections commute with restriction. Hence the two edge maps commute with restriction. This uses the existing cocycle statement rather than assuming functoriality in the second functor of the Grothendieck spectral sequence.

old_proof.text: For each etale $W\to U$, set $C=Z_U\times_UW$ and $O=W\setminus C$. Apply [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] both on $W$ and on $O$. The derived unit identifies the ordinary etale and pro-etale cohomology of the finite coefficient sheaf $A(r)$ on each, compatibly with restriction. The functorial support long exact sequences on both sites in [thm-pur-with-support-exactness] now form a commutative diagram. In the five-term segment $H^{d-1}(W)\to H^{d-1}(O)\to H^d_C(W)\to H^d(W)\to H^d(O)$, all four ordinary-cohomology comparison arrows are isomorphisms; the five lemma gives the middle supported comparison. Taking $d=2c$ transfers the edge isomorphism of Step 6 (or Step 1) to the pro-etale left side. Naturality of the unit and support sequences makes this comparison commute with every further etale restriction.

old_proof.text: Let two degree-$2c$ supported classes have equal restrictions to an etale covering of $U$. By the natural edge isomorphism in Step 6 (Step 1 if $c=0$), their images are sections of $\mathcal H^{2c}_{Z_U}(A(r))$ agreeing on that cover. The sheaf separation axiom makes the images equal globally; injectivity of the edge makes the original classes equal. No identification of this sheaf with a constant or twist sheaf, and no orientation or frame-independence assertion, is used.
